convertibility_reason: Uses only standard MT5 functions (CopyRates, CopyHigh, CopyLow, no iCustom calls). Entry/exit rules are simple. Fixed lot sizing. Standard library includes (Trade\*.mqh) have Python equivalents. No custom indicators, no external trading logic libraries, no grid/martingale.

derived_values.name: OpCl: 24-bar open minus 1-bar close (cumulative rollback up)
ClOp: 1-bar close minus 24-bar open (cumulative rollback down)
ClLo: 1-bar close minus 25-bar lowest low
derived_values.used_by: Not directly used in entry (computed but unused)

derived_values.name: HiCl: 25-bar highest high minus 1-bar close
derived_values.used_by: Not directly used in entry (computed but unused)

other_exits: Time-based forced close: all positions closed when hour==22 and min>45

custom_logic_notes: Entry window restricted to day_of_week==InpDayOfWeek (default Friday), hour==0, min<=3. The EA measures price rollback over 24 bars: long if price has rolled down sufficiently (open[24]-close[1] > corridor), short if price has rolled up sufficiently (close[1]-open[24] > corridor). SL/TP are set relative to current bar open price (OpD=rates[0].open). ClLo and HiCl are computed but not used in entry decisions. Forced close at 22:45 each day.
python_conversion_notes: Simple rollback strategy. Key logic: measure cumulative price movement over 24 bars, enter if rollback exceeds corridor threshold. Time filter restricts entry to a specific day at midnight. Trailing stop activates after profit exceeds trailing_stop+trailing_step. Standard Trade library classes map to simple broker API calls in Python. The iHighest/iLowest helper functions need reimplementation as rolling max/min over lookback window. Note: ClLo and HiCl variables are computed but unused - can be omitted in Python.
